mainTopic: Whether נידוי and שמתא wording can work as a נדר, and related rules about נידוי
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב פפא's explanation that רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about the phrase 'מנודה אני לך'. רבי עקיבא hears it as distancing wording, which can be a נדר, while the רבנן hear it as excommunication wording. The גמרא then shows from a story that רב חסדא holds differently: they argue even about 'משמתנא'. Next come teachings of רב about נידוי. A נידוי given to a person's face is lifted only to his face, and one who hears God's name said in vain must put the speaker in נידוי, because such talk brings poverty, which counts like death. A story about רב הונא backs up these rules and teaches that a נידוי may be lifted right away. רב also teaches that a תלמיד חכם may put himself in נידוי and lift it himself, as מר זוטרא חסידא did. The amud ends as רב גידל begins another teaching of רב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where רבי עקיבא and the רבנן really disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes his explanation: the argument is about the phrase 'מנודה אני לך'. רבי עקיבא hears it as distancing wording, which can be a נדר. The רבנן hear it as excommunication wording, which is not a נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about 'I am מנודה to you.' רבי עקיבא holds that this is wording of distancing. The רבנן hold that it is wording of excommunication.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's statement. He says the real argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן is about the phrase 'מנודה אני לך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what the word מנודה really means when a person uses it. רבי עקיבא says it means 'I keep away from you', so it works like a נדר. The רבנן say it is the language of שמתא (excommunication), which is not how people make נדרים, so it does not create a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Wording of distancing or keeping away
The Rabbis, meaning the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'נידויא' does not mean the court's punishment of נידוי. רבי עקיבא understands it as plain distancing, like a person saying 'I stay away from you', and that is why it can work as a נדר.

phrases.english: [They argue] about 'I am ostracized from you,'
for Rabbi Akiva holds:
it is language of distancing,
and the Rabbis hold:
it is language of excommunication.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לִישָּׁנָא דְנִידּוּיָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's statement, which began before this section, about where the תנאים disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about 'מנודה אני לך'. רבי עקיבא treats it as distancing (a נדר), and the רבנן treat it as excommunication wording (not a נדר).

steps.title: A story showing רב חסדא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב פפא's view goes against רב חסדא. It proves this from a man who said 'משמתנא' about someone's property. רב חסדא told him that nobody follows רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רב חסדא. A man said, 'I am excommunicated from the property of the son of רב ירמיה בר אבא.' He came before רב חסדא, who told him: 'Nobody takes this opinion of רבי עקיבא into account.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב פפא's explanation clashes with רב חסדא. It brings a story about a ruling רב חסדא gave to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, the man used the word משמתנא, not מנודה. רב חסדא still treated the case as if רבי עקיבא would have called it a נדר, and he only rejected it because the הלכה does not follow רבי עקיבא. That would not fit רב פפא, who said everyone agrees משמתנא is not a נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no one who is concerned for it

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Chisda.
For a certain man who said,
'I am excommunicated from the property'
of the son of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba,'
came before Rav Chisda.
He said to him: There is no one who is concerned
for this view of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that another אמורא understood the scope of the argument differently from רב פפא.
steps.raayaObject: That רב חסדא held a different view from רב פפא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling on a man who said 'משמתנא' about someone's property

steps.title: רב חסדא holds they argue even about 'excommunicated'
steps.stepSummary: From the story, the גמרא concludes that רב חסדא holds רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue even about the word 'משמתנא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that they argue about 'I am excommunicated' too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the story teaches about רב חסדא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא only needed to say 'we do not follow רבי עקיבא' if רבי עקיבא would call משמתנא a נדר. So for רב חסדא, the argument is about the whole group of ostracism and excommunication words. It is not limited to the single phrase 'מנודה אני לך', as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this tells us his opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: the תנאים argue only about 'מנודה', and everyone agrees 'משמתנא' is not a נדר. רב חסדא: they argue even about 'משמתנא', and the הלכה does not follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: He holds: they disagree about 'I am excommunicated.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the logical inference from רב חסדא's ruling in the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא holds that the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן covers 'משמתנא' too, which goes against רב פפא.

steps.title: Lifting a נידוי in or out of the person's presence
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a נידוי given to a person's face can only be lifted to his face. A נידוי given when he was not there can be lifted either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said in the name of רב: If he put him in נידוי in his presence, they may lift it only in his presence. If he put him in נידוי not in his presence, they may lift it either in his presence or not in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רב about how a נידוי is lifted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How the נידוי is lifted depends on how it was given. If it was done to the person's face, it must be lifted to his face. If it was done when he was not there, there is no such requirement, so it can be lifted either way.

keyTerms.meaning: He put him in נידוי (ostracized him)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila said that Rav said:
If he ostracized him in his presence,
they may lift it for him only in his presence.
If he ostracized him not in his presence,
they may lift it for him either in his presence
or not in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from נידוי wording in נדרים to the laws of נידוי itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נידוי given in a person's presence can be lifted only in his presence. One given in his absence can be lifted either way.

steps.title: Hearing God's name said in vain
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a person who hears someone say הזכרת השם in vain must put him in נידוי. If he does not, the listener himself deserves נידוי, because where God's name is used in vain, poverty is common.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנין said in the name of רב: One who hears his friend mention God's name in vain must put him in נידוי. If he does not, he himself should be in נידוי. This is because wherever mentioning God's name in vain is common, poverty is common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב about נידוי. It says when a listener must put a speaker in נידוי, and it gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listener has a duty to protest, and he is held responsible if he stays silent. The reason given is that using God's name in vain brings poverty to the whole place. So stopping it protects everyone, not just the speaker.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows that נידוי is used to protect respect for God's name, and that a bystander who stays silent shares the responsibility.

phrases.english: Rav Chanin said that Rav said:
One who hears mention of God's name from his friend's mouth
phrases.notes: This means saying God's name for no purpose, in vain. The גמרא assumes this without spelling it out.

phrases.english: must ostracize him,
and if he did not ostracize him,
he himself shall be ostracized.
For wherever mention of God's name is common,
there poverty is common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רב about נידוי, following the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who hears God's name said in vain must put the speaker in נידוי. If he fails to, he himself deserves נידוי.

steps.title: Poverty is like death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues רב's warning about poverty. It shows that poverty is treated like death, from a פסוק and from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And poverty is like death. The פסוק says 'for all the men are dead,' and a ברייתא teaches that wherever the Sages set their eyes on someone, the result was either death or poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the poverty mentioned in step 5 is so serious. It brings two proofs that poverty counts like death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רב said poverty comes where God's name is used in vain. Here the גמרא adds how harsh that is: poverty is put on the same level as death. The פסוק calls living people 'dead,' and the ברייתא puts death and poverty side by side as the same kind of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages set their eyes on someone (looked at him harshly)

phrases.english: And poverty is like death,
as it is said: "For all the men are dead,"
phrases.notes: שמות 4:19. The idea is that these men were still alive but had become poor, so 'dead' here means poor.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a ברייתא:
Wherever "the Sages set their eyes" on someone,
the result was either death or poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reason given at the end of step 5 by proving that poverty is as severe as death.
steps.raayaObject: That poverty is treated like death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'כי מתו כל האנשים' and a ברייתא about the Sages setting their eyes on someone

steps.title: רב הונא puts a woman in נידוי and lifts it at once
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells how רב הונא heard a woman say God's name in vain. He put her in שמתא and right away lifted it, in front of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: I was standing in front of רב הונא. He heard a woman say God's name in vain. He put her in שמתא and immediately lifted it for her, in her presence.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא tells a real-life story of רב הונא. This story sets up the next step, where the גמרא learns three rules from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story has three details: רב הונא put her in נידוי, he lifted it in front of her, and he lifted it immediately. Each detail will become its own lesson in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He put her in שמתא (a form of נידוי)
In her presence, to her face

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
I was standing before Rav Huna,
he heard a certain woman
who uttered a mention of God's name in vain,
he put her in שמתא and released it for her immediately, in her presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that fits רב's rules from steps 4 and 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rules about נידוי for saying God's name in vain and how to lift it
steps.raayaSupportSource: What רבי אבא saw רב הונא do

steps.title: Three lessons from רב הונא's story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns three things from the story: one who hears God's name said in vain must put the speaker in נידוי; a נידוי given to someone's face is lifted only to his face; and no waiting time is needed before lifting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. One who hears his friend say God's name in vain must put him in נידוי. If someone was put in נידוי in his presence, it can be lifted only in his presence. And there is no gap at all needed between the נידוי and lifting it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three rules out of the story of רב הונא. Each detail of what he did teaches one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting her in נידוי supports רב's rule in step 5. Lifting it in front of her supports רב's rule in step 4. Lifting it right away is a new lesson: a נידוי does not have to last any minimum time before it is lifted.
steps.whatToRemember: From רב הונא's story we learn three rules: (1) hearing God's name in vain requires נידוי, (2) a face-to-face נידוי is lifted face-to-face, (3) it can be lifted immediately.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things:
Learn from this: one who hears a mention of God's name
from his fellow's mouth must put him in נידוי,
and learn from this: if he put him in נידוי in his presence,
they may release it for him only in his presence,
and learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין נִידּוּי לַהֲפָרָה וְלֹא כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: there is nothing at all between נידוי and its cancellation.
phrases.notes: No waiting time is needed: you can lift the נידוי right after giving it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lessons out of the story told in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story supports רב's two rules and adds that a נידוי can be lifted immediately.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם can put himself in נידוי and lift it
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: a תלמיד חכם may put himself in נידוי, and he may also lift it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: A תלמיד חכם can put himself in נידוי, and he can lift it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב says a Torah scholar can give himself a נידוי and also take it off himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we spoke about putting someone else in נידוי. Here רב adds that a תלמיד חכם can do both sides by himself: give the נידוי and lift it.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
A Torah scholar may put himself in נידוי,
and he may cancel it for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new rule about נידוי: doing it to oneself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may put himself in נידוי and lift it himself.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this. If a scholar can lift a נידוי for others, surely he can lift it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's teaching as something we already would have known. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that רב's teaching seems to add nothing. A scholar can put others in נידוי and lift it for them, so why would he not be able to do the same for himself?

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב's teaching in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's teaching that a תלמיד חכם can put himself in נידוי and lift it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he can do it for others, the same power should obviously work for himself, so the teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A prisoner cannot free himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we might have thought a person in נידוי is like a prisoner, who cannot free himself. רב teaches that he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: 'A prisoner cannot free himself from prison.' So רב teaches us that he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a good reason to think the opposite. That is why רב had to teach the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the scholar is in נידוי, he is 'locked in,' and we might think someone locked in cannot unlock himself. רב tells us this saying does not apply here, and the scholar may lift his own נידוי.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
"A prisoner cannot free himself from prison,"
it teaches us that he can.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Someone in נידוי is like a prisoner and cannot release himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תלמיד חכם can lift his own נידוי.

steps.title: When would this happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of situation would lead a scholar to put himself in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real example of a scholar putting himself in נידוי. This sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds strange for someone to give himself a נידוי. The גמרא wants a concrete case where this actually makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical example of רב's rule from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real situation where a תלמיד חכם would put himself in נידוי

steps.title: The practice of מר זוטרא חסידא
steps.stepSummary: When a student deserved נידוי, מר זוטרא חסידא first put himself in נידוי and then the student. At home he first lifted his own and then the student's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like מר זוטרא חסידא: when a student of the academy deserved שמתא, he first put himself in שמתא and then put the student in שמתא. When he went into his house, he released himself first, and then released the student.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the example of מר זוטרא חסידא, who put himself in נידוי together with a student who deserved it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא did not want to punish a student without sharing the punishment himself, so he gave himself the נידוי first. This is exactly the case רב was talking about. He also lifted his own נידוי by himself, just as רב said a scholar may do.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם may put himself in נידוי and lift it himself, as מר זוטרא חסידא did whenever he had to put a student in נידוי.

phrases.english: Like that of Mar Zutra the pious:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִחַיַּיב בַּר בֵּי רַב שַׁמְתָּא —
phrases.english: when a student of the academy deserved שמתא,
he would first put himself in שמתא,
and then put the student in שמתא.
And when he went into his house,
he would release himself, and then release the student.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a real example.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מר זוטרא חסידא put himself in נידוי before putting a student in נידוי, and lifted his own before lifting the student's.

steps.title: Introducing another teaching from רב גידל in the name of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement that רב גידל says in the name of רב. This line only names who is speaking. The content comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב גידל said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It tells us who is speaking before we hear what he says: רב גידל, quoting his teacher רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "and" (וְ) links this to the earlier statement from the same pair in step 9, where a scholar may put himself in נידוי. That story is finished. The גמרא is now adding another teaching from the same teachers. Nothing has been ruled yet; this is only the opening.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he said." The "and" shows this is one more teaching from the same speaker as before.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in this line. It is only the opening. The actual teaching starts right after the colon.

phrases.english: And Rav Giddel said
that Rav said:

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None. This is the opening of a new מימרא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story of מר זוטרא חסידא (step 13) is finished. The גמרא now turns to another teaching from the same speakers as step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only says who the speakers are; the teaching itself follows.
